data.name: Rivka
data.gender_notes: Rivka is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rivka, derived from the Hebrew word 'riv,' meaning 'to see,' and 'ka,' meaning 'God.' This name signifies 'God's Creatress' or 'God's Seer.' It's also associated with the biblical character Rebecca, a matriarch in the Old Testament. The name Rivka carries the meaning “God's Creatress” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rivka usually hope their child will grow to embody god's creatress and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name connected to the divine and the gift of sight.
data.etymology: Rivka belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Creatress.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rivka total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: ריבקה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ריבקה הוא השם העברי הנשי שמשמעותו 'לאסוף או לקשור מארבעת הצדדים', ומקורו בשם העברי רבה שמשמעותו 'רב' או 'גדול'. השם ריבקה מוזכר בספר בראשית כהבתו של אבימלעך ובת דודו של אברהם. היא אישה יפה ובעלת מוסר גבוה, שזכתה להינשא ליצחק וללדת תאומים, עשו ויעקב.

in_greek.name: Ριβκά
in_greek.meaning: να συνδέσει ή να δέσει από τις τέσσερις πλευρές
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ριβκά στην ελληνική παράδοση προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα ריבקה, που σημαίνει 'να συνδέσει ή να δέσει από τις τέσσερις πλευρές'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη δεν αναφέρεται συγκεκριμένα το όνομα Ριβκά, αλλά η Ριβκά της Παλαιάς Διαθήκης αναφέρεται ως παράδειγμα γυναικών με πίστη και αρετή.

in_latin.name: Rivka
in_latin.meaning: to bind or tie from four sides
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Rivka originates from the Hebrew name ריבקה, meaning 'to bind or tie from four sides'. This name holds significance in the biblical context as Rebecca, the wife of Isaac and mother of Esau and Jacob, exemplifying faith and virtue. The Latin Church has traditionally recognized the importance of biblical names in Christian heritage.
